sample_rule: Predefined first five evaluation trials (0–4) for each training seed 101 and 111, selected before viewing; 10 videos total.
method: Manual visual review of 8 equally spaced full-scene frames per video, plus 8 enlarged intermediate frames for each of the six failed videos. This is a qualitative subset diagnosis, not official evaluation labels or an estimate of full-evaluation success rate.

contact_sheet_method.full_scene: Eight indices round(i*(n_frames-1)/7), i=0..7; resized480x270 with captions; 4 columns ×2 rows.
contact_sheet_method.first_frame_note: First frame of trial0 is black in each original video. Other frames were used for diagnosis.

interpretation: The observed failure region is acquisition: near-object alignment/approach and grasp, before stable lift. These videos do not justify classifying all failures specifically as grasp, nor do they prove that limited source-demonstration coverage is the cause. Increased coverage via Mimic is a testable hypothesis, not an established diagnosis.
limitations: Only first5trial perseed were manually reviewed; not the entire100trial sets.
Only RGB video sampled frames are available; exact contacts, commanded gripper state, and official success predicate outputs are absent.
Trials3/4 are visually completed but remain separate from official success counters until stdout or definitive result evidence is supplied.
Do not infer success from video duration.

trials.confidence: high for no acquisition; limited for approach-versus-grasp split
observed_evidence: The gripper approaches the toy vicinity but remains visibly offset during the near-object motion.
The hand subsequently rises and moves away without the toy; the toy remains on the tabletop in later and final frames.
No stable lift or loaded transport is visible. Sparse RGB frames do not establish the exact gripper-close action or 3D clearance.
The gripper reaches the toy and repeatedly works at tabletop height near it (about 8–24 s).
The toy is left on the table while the hand rises away empty (about 28–40 s).
No sustained lifted transport of the toy to the box is visible.

trials.confidence: high for visual task completion; official predicate output unavailable
observed_evidence: The toy is visibly acquired and lifted from the tabletop.
The gripper carries the toy toward the box; the final frame shows the toy inside the box after release.
